title: Your AI agents can now control your Google Home devices
slides: Google Home now lets AI agents control your devices
But only through a new integration layer
Your lights, thermostat, and locks become agent tools
You'll need to reauthorize each device manually
Audit your automations before agents run wild
thread_text:
1. AI Agents Now Control Your Home

Google Home just gave AI agents the keys to your lights, thermostat, and locks. But there's a catch you need to see.

2. The Integration Layer Twist

A new layer sits between your devices and the AI. It decides what agents can touch—and what they can't.

3. Your Devices as Tools

Every smart bulb, lock, and thermostat becomes a tool an agent can call. Imagine an AI locking your door at 3 AM.

4. Reauthorize Every Device

You'll have to manually reauthorize each device. Miss one, and the agent loses access—or keeps it. Check your list.

5. Audit Before Agents Run Wild

Open your Google Home app and review every automation today. Uncheck anything you wouldn't want an AI to trigger accidentally.

instagram.caption:
Your smart lock just became something an AI agent can trigger while you sleep.

Google Home now lets AI agents control your lights, thermostat, and locks. 🔐

A new integration layer sits between your devices and the AI, deciding what agents can actually touch.

Every bulb and lock becomes a tool an agent can call. But you have to reauthorize each device manually first.

If you run automations for work or content, open your Home app today and review what's connected. Miss one device, and an agent keeps access you forgot about.

Which device would you never hand to an agent? 🤖
